title: HTTP caching: Cache-Control, ETag and conditional validation

videos.script: A visitor opens a book page. The browser asks for the page, the stylesheet, the script, the logo, and the book. {{assets}} Most of those answers have not changed since yesterday. Asking for them again costs a round trip each, and the book costs a query to a slow database. {{again}} HTTP has a way to say: keep this copy, and for how long. A browser keeps it for one person. A proxy in front of the application keeps it for everybody. {{copies}} When the time runs out, the copy is not thrown away. The cache asks a smaller question. Has this changed? If not, the answer is three hundred and four, and no body. {{ask}} In this lesson you write those instructions into the bookshop's responses, turn Nginx into a shared cache, and count how many times the database is spared. {{count}} And you find the request that a shared cache should never answer from its copy, because the copy belongs to somebody else. {{private}}
